narrative_purpose: A label-ready soil aggregate cutaway shows why millimetres matter: mineral architecture, water films, gas-filled pores and an oxygen-poor core produce different microbial habitats side by side.
subject: One irregular dark soil aggregate shown as a large clean cutaway, built from distinct sand, silt and clay grains bound by pale fungal threads, hair-fine roots and translucent microbial glue. Open pores wind through it. Thin cyan water films coat grains near the outer surface while one deeper pore is fully water-filled and darker. Small clusters of rod and sphere microbes occupy the films, with a visibly dim oxygen-poor inner core.
scene: The isolated aggregate floats against a plain deep-indigo specimen field, with only a faint bed of loose grains below.
camera: Straight-on macro cutaway, aggregate filling the middle two-thirds of frame, outer pore at upper left and darker core at lower right clearly separated.
light: Cool cyan light tracing thin water films, living-teal microbial pinpoints, soft mineral highlights, the inner saturated core visibly darker and muted.
palette: Void-indigo background, charcoal and mineral grey grains, cyan water, teal biology, faint amber organic fragments.
style: Painterly scientific specimen plate with clear anatomy and hand-painted texture, not a vector infographic.
detail_level: Crisp grain boundaries, films, hyphae, pores and microbial clusters; simple dark background reserved for overlay labels.
composition: Large centered aggregate with three legible zones—outer gas-filled pore, connected water-film middle, dark saturated core—and open margins around each.
consistency_notes: Use spatial architecture, water thickness and brightness to encode the pore gradient. No baked labels or arrows; interface annotations will identify features.
